title: Garash cake (Bulgarian chocolate and walnut torte)

ingredients.name: dark chocolate and 50 ml cream for the glaze

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C (160 C fan) and line the base of a 24 cm springform tin. Beat the egg whites with half of the sugar until they hold stiff, glossy peaks.
In another bowl, beat the yolks with the remaining sugar and the vanilla until pale and thick. Fold in the ground walnuts and cocoa.
Gently fold the egg whites into the yolk mixture in two batches, keeping as much air as possible, then divide it between three lined tins, or bake it in one tin and split it later.
Bake for about 20 minutes for thin layers, or 35 minutes for a single cake, until springy. Cool completely.
For the cream, melt the 200 g chocolate and let it cool a little. Beat the butter with the icing sugar until fluffy, then beat in the chocolate and the milk.
Sandwich the layers with the chocolate cream and spread the rest over the top and sides. Chill for 30 minutes.
For the glaze, heat the cream, pour it over the chopped 100 g chocolate and stir until smooth. Pour it over the cake, let it set in the fridge, and serve in thin slices.

title: Kebapche (Bulgarian grilled minced meat sausages)

ingredients.name: lyutenitsa (or ajvar), chips and grated sirene or feta to serve

steps: Combine both minces in a large bowl with the salt, pepper, cumin, paprika and baking soda.
Knead the meat for about 5 minutes, adding the water a spoonful at a time, until the mixture turns sticky and cohesive.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight, so the flavours develop and the meat firms up.
With wet hands, shape portions of about 80 g into short, thick cylinders.
Heat a grill or griddle pan until very hot and cook the kebapche for about 4 minutes per side, turning once or twice, until nicely charred outside and cooked through.
Serve at once with chips scattered with grated sirene, a spoonful of lyutenitsa, fresh onion and bread.

title: Lyutenitsa (Bulgarian roasted pepper and tomato relish)

ingredients.name: red bell peppers (ideally long red peppers)

steps: Roast the whole peppers and aubergine under a hot grill or in a 230 C oven until the skins are blackened, then put them in a covered bowl to steam for 15 minutes.
Peel off the skins and remove the seeds from the peppers; scrape the aubergine flesh from its skin. Briefly blanch the tomatoes, peel them and chop them.
Process the peppers, aubergine and tomatoes coarsely, or put them through a mincer, for a rustic texture.
Warm half of the oil in a wide, heavy pot, add the carrots and cook for a few minutes, then add the vegetable puree.
Simmer uncovered over low heat for about 1 to 1.5 hours, stirring often, until the relish is thick enough to hold a spoon trail.

Stir in the garlic, sugar, salt, chilli and the remaining oil and cook for 10 minutes more. Cool and serve on bread, with grilled meat or in cheese sandwiches; it keeps for a week in the fridge, or longer if sterilised in jars.

title: Mekitsi (Bulgarian fried yogurt dough)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for dusting
icing sugar, jam or crumbled sirene (or feta) to serve

steps: Stir the yogurt, egg, baking soda and salt together in a bowl; the soda will react and make the mixture lightly foamy.
Add the flour a little at a time and work it into a soft, slightly sticky dough, using the warm water only as needed. Do not knead it hard.
Cover the dough and leave it to rest for about 30 minutes.
Heat the oil in a deep frying pan over medium heat to about 175 C. Oil your hands, pull off egg-sized pieces of dough, and stretch them gently into flat rounds or ovals.
Fry the mekitsi a couple at a time, 1 to 2 minutes per side, until puffed and golden brown. Lift out and drain on kitchen paper.
Serve warm, dusted with icing sugar or spread with jam, or with crumbled white cheese for a savoury version.

title: Mish-mash (Bulgarian pepper, tomato and cheese scramble)

ingredients.name: green peppers (long mild Bulgarian type, or any mild pepper), sliced

steps: Heat the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion for about 3 minutes until soft.
Add the sliced peppers and fry for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until they soften.
Add the diced tomatoes with a little salt and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the vegetables are soft and most of the juice has cooked off.
Lightly beat the eggs with half of the crumbled cheese, then pour them over the vegetables.
Stir gently over low heat until the eggs are just set but still moist, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Scatter over the remaining cheese and the parsley, taste before adding more salt since the cheese is salty, and serve warm with bread.

title: Panagyurishte-style eggs (poached eggs on garlic yogurt and cheese)

ingredients.name: white vinegar, for the poaching water

steps: Stir the yogurt with the crushed garlic and a pinch of salt in a bowl, then fold in half of the crumbled cheese. Let it stand at room temperature.
Bring a wide pan of water to a gentle simmer and add the vinegar. Crack each egg into a cup and slide it into the water one at a time.
Poach the eggs for about 3 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft, then lift them out with a slotted spoon and drain briefly.
Warm the yogurt mixture very gently in a pan or just set it in a serving dish; keep it barely warm, since too much heat makes yogurt split.
Place the poached eggs on top of the yogurt and scatter over the rest of the cheese.
Melt the butter in a small pan until it foams, stir in the paprika for a few seconds, and pour it over the eggs. Serve right away with toasted bread.

title: Patatnik (Rhodope grated potato pie)

ingredients.name: sunflower oil, plus extra for the dish
plain flour (only if the mixture is very wet)

steps: Heat the oven to 200 C (180 C fan) and oil a round baking dish or tin of about 26 cm.
Coarsely grate the potatoes and squeeze them hard in a clean cloth to remove the liquid; keep the starchy liquid that settles at the bottom and tip it back in.
Mix the potatoes with the onion, mint, paprika, salt and 3 tablespoons of oil. If the mixture seems loose, stir in the flour.
Set aside about a third of the mixture. Press the rest into the dish, building up the sides a little.
Spoon the remaining potato mixture on top and flatten it, pinching the edges together to seal like a pie.
Brush the top with the remaining oil and bake for 45 to 55 minutes, until the surface is crusty and golden and the potatoes are cooked through.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting; serve warm with yogurt or a tomato salad.

title: Zelnik (Bulgarian layered pastry with leeks and cheese)

ingredients.name: sunflower oil, for brushing the sheets
black pepper, and salt only if needed

steps: Heat 3 tablespoons of oil in a large pan and cook the leeks for about 10 minutes until very soft, then let them cool completely. If using spinach, wilt it, squeeze it dry and chop it.
Beat the eggs with the yogurt and the baking soda, then stir in the cooled leeks, the crumbled cheese and plenty of black pepper. Taste before adding salt, as the cheese is salty.
Heat the oven to 190 C (170 C fan) and oil a large baking dish.
Lay a sheet of filo in the dish, brush it with oil, and repeat with 4 more sheets, letting the edges hang over.
Spread half of the filling over the pastry, add 2 or 3 more oiled sheets, then the rest of the filling.
Cover with the remaining filo, oiling every sheet, and fold the overhanging edges over the top. Brush the top well with oil and score it into squares.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until deep golden. Let it rest for 10 minutes, then cut and serve warm or cold with yogurt.
